text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday its third quarter business performance was "most disappointing".
"The anticipated recovery of sales and income has not materialised," it said in a statement.
The Dutch electronics giant earlier posted third quarter net profit from normal operations of 123 million guilders, down from 539 million a year earlier.
Philips said income from normal operations more than halved in the first nine months of 1996 to 804 million guilders, or 2.35 guilders per share.

"In addition to the lower than expected sales growth and increasing price erosion in various markets, income was affected by unfavourable developments particularly in the semiconductor industry and in passive components, and the costs associated with our entry into the consumer communications business," it said.
Philips said comparable sales growth for the group in the nine months was six percent versus 12 percent a year earlier.
Price erosion was four percent compared with two peercent in the same 1995 period.
Finance costs climbed to 684 million guilders from 600 million reflecting the rising cost of servicing the increased debt load, the group said.
